audit.whatIsWrong: The packet itself flags it: Yasuo wins 53.43% but the chart hands Irelia 6 of 7 stages, including 2+ items where the page's own whys[6] says Yasuo out-scales her.
audit.why: The mirror set Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Irelia, Skill, Yasuo across both layers. Rows 1-5 already match; rows 0 and 6 do not. whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] also carry the wrong stage labels (Level 4 / Level 5 / Level 6 against rows Levels 4-5 / Level 6 / First item).
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 6 flipped in both layers with ratings rescaled; whys[0], whys[3], whys[4], whys[5] rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero sequencing cues — no cooldown numbers anywhere.
audit.why: Bladesurge 10/9/8/7/6, Defiant Dance 20/18/16/14/12, Flawless Duet 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85, Wind Wall 25s at rank 1, Last Breath 70/50/30.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0..3], early, mid, whys[0], phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance's physical damage reduction is never mentioned, Vanguard's Edge is not identified as equally wall-blockable, and 'Last Breath converts ANY knockup' is false here.
audit.why: Defiant Dance reduces the physical damage she takes while charging — your crit autos and Steel Tempest are physical, so dumping a trade into a charged W is the single most common way this lane is lost. Both Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge carry the projectile flag, so one 4-second Wind Wall answers her stun AND her ultimate engage; the mirror reached the same conclusion. Nothing in her kit knocks her airborne, so Last Breath follows only your own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind.
audit.corrected: W damage reduction stated with its 20s cooldown; Wind Wall pointed at both E and R; Q2 whirlwind named as the only Last Breath setup.

audit.whatIsWrong: The item line says 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern'.
audit.why: Yasuo has no healing. The heal is Irelia's, off Bladesurge, and it refreshes on every reset — which is exactly why anti-heal is right here.
audit.corrected: Reason rewritten to name Bladesurge's healing.

edits.after: Vanguard's Edge (R) is 125s at rank 1 and its blades are projectiles — Wind Wall eats the whole engage. Bait Defiant Dance (W) first; it cuts your physical damage.

edits.before: Irelia's on-hit spike with full passive stacks beats your crit until you complete a second item; Wind Wall her Flawless Duet (E) stun projectiles to survive her all-in.

edits.before: You finally out-scale her once your crit fully outpaces her stack-dependent damage; Wind Wall the E stun and R knock-back, then Q3 into Last Breath when she can't Bladesurge away.
edits.after: You out-scale her once crit outpaces her stacks; Wind Wall eats both Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge, then take your Q2 whirlwind into Last Breath when she has no minion to Bladesurge to.

edits.before: Irelia beats you at every early level — Bladesurge (Q) resets on marked minions let her close, stack her passive, and out-trade you before you have crit. Freeze or manage the wave so she has no low minions to reset onto, and never trade into a full four-stack passive.
edits.after: Irelia beats you from level 2 onward — Bladesurge (Q, 10s at rank 1) resets on marked minions let her close, stack her passive, and heal off each hit. Freeze or manage the wave so she has no low minions to reset onto, buy Grievous Wounds, and never trade into a full-stack passive.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay firmly Irelia's: her passive attack-speed stacks and Flawless Duet (E) stun make every all-in favor her, and even at 6 her stacked damage out-DPS your ult trade. This is a survival phase — farm safe, Wind Wall the E, and don't feed Bladesurge resets.
edits.after: Levels 2-6 stay firmly Irelia's: her passive attack-speed stacks and the Flawless Duet (E) stun on 16s at rank 1 make every all-in favour her. This is a survival phase — farm safe, Wind Wall the E blades outright, bait the 20s Defiant Dance, and never feed a Bladesurge reset.

edits.before: Only at 2+ items does the matchup flip to you, when your crit finally outpaces her stack-dependent on-hit. Wind Wall her Flawless Duet stun and Vanguard's Edge (R) knock-back, then land Q3 into Last Breath while she has no minion to Bladesurge away to.
edits.after: Only at two items does the matchup flip, when your crit outpaces her stack-dependent on-hit. Wind Wall eats Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge alike, so bait both, then land your own Q2 whirlwind into Last Breath while she has no minion to Bladesurge to.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Irelia's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Last Breath (70s at rank 1) fires only off your own Q2 whirlwind. Vanguard's Edge is 125s and Wind Wall eats it.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Irelia carry threat: 9/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Last Breath needs an airborne target and only your own Q2 whirlwind supplies one. Irelia carry threat: 9/10 — anti-heal against Bladesurge stays core; shift to picks if she leads.
